### 2026-10-03 — This is the project I have been working on for a long time now. It is an ESP32-based inventory manager and dashboard. Its primary purpose is to help me keep timers for studying, Pomodoro, and other ac

**4.7h**

This is the project I have been working on for a long time now. It is an ESP32-based inventory manager and dashboard. Its primary purpose is to help me keep timers for studying, Pomodoro, and other activities. In addition, it tells me the location of almost 230 modules I own.

![IMG_20260930_161512](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/rWl10s59mLisg4XtHMiy6Tgh5DzAJl32/650c5c4382daee9d6746028784166092bba1bce4c0eaa426635156d4dff0e2db.jpg)

![IMG_20260927_155842](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/rWl10s59mLisg4XtHMiy6Tgh5DzAJl32/7222e5f6849d9b48b04015c20736288fb1fc3e4612f529188857e1a8c95ec2ba.jpg)

Looking into the details, I have an ESP32 as the main microcontroller, and I use most of its functionalities except Bluetooth. Next, we have the SSD1306 OLED module. I am looking to update it to a TFT display because the current OLED display is relatively small and difficult to see while sitting at my bench. The OLED display is followed by a small button, a toggle switch that I can use to turn it on and off, and an RTC module to track the time correctly because I will not be keeping the device turned on continuously, as I only have a 2,200 mAh battery in it.

Next, we have the most important part, of course: the keypad module. This is a 4-by-4 keypad module in which I have introduced a Nokia-style button keypad. Pressing a single button multiple times triggers a letter. For example, pressing button 5 twice gives the letter K.

During this specific session, I integrated the RTC module because, in the previous version, the RTC module was not working at all. It was not even being detected. I diagnosed the problem as the SDA and SCL lines being switched. I was also sharing those SDA and SCL lines with my OLED module. I changed that from pin 2 to pins 16 and 17, and used the SDA and SCL lines for the RTC module.

![17910094699313928562183987608223](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/rWl10s59mLisg4XtHMiy6Tgh5DzAJl32/d0f93282bba0a94ae72e19c8b3d97763289ffd92581db19bc1daa611b356dbba.jpg)

Integrating this RTC module was quite a bit of work because I had never interfaced any of my microcontrollers with an RTC module before. I first wrote a test sketch and was able to retrieve almost all the details, but the time was offset. I bought a new coin cell for it because the old one was nearly dead. In the sketch I wrote, I updated the time to the correct date and hour.

![Screenshot_20261003-121354](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/rWl10s59mLisg4XtHMiy6Tgh5DzAJl32/ff7e4210de97bcde8a7456d0251fb31a7e39ce167923f168f5d9ac9d3561fcd2.png)

The next thing I did during this session was secure the connections so that the previous issue of the keypad module disconnecting automatically would be resolved. In addition, I made many software changes. The ESP32 was consuming a lot of power because the OLED module was turned on at all times, and it was calculating time in three to four layers simultaneously. To reduce that, I implemented light sleep, which is a step below deep sleep. In light sleep, only the OLED module stays active, and if a clock is needed, the RTC module is also used. However, the anti-semodule consumes very little power, which is negligible. By using this and reducing the loop cycle, I was successfully able to reduce the current consumption and thereby increase the lifespan of the device.

![Screenshot_20261003-121342](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/rWl10s59mLisg4XtHMiy6Tgh5DzAJl32/78e3bc7ec725093219a9ccbfba8985a5483958cb52b0778b62ff1d2246785941.png)

In the next session, I am looking forward to adding an INMP441 microphone module so that I can talk to this module like an agent and trigger it by calling its name, such as, “Hey, Jarvis.” It will then turn on, and I will be able to command it by saying, “Hey, Jarvis, go to the inventory. I also want to take an OLED module with an ESP32-CAM "   the agent inside my ESP32 will update the LittleFS storage, allowing me to do that hands-free.(The blank space below the oled is reserved for future modules,including inmp441  ,vibration motor,etc)

![IMG_20260930_153809](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/rWl10s59mLisg4XtHMiy6Tgh5DzAJl32/68fd92502b7e43123a5c07901af99b6899d6f12cdcdf34d904e046a395c5afbe.jpg)

![Screenshot_20261003-121319](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/rWl10s59mLisg4XtHMiy6Tgh5DzAJl32/1aad7c451c4f82596a659a68ce04ce2ac3167ddfb67667faad9cb5f3dea99209.png)

(Sorry for the crappy images,my cam is cooked yall🥀✌🏻,also had to take a vedio and ss from it since memory on ts shi is cooked too)

That’s all for this session.

### 2026-10-03 — https://github.com/Ajmaleee/CircuitShelf

**6.3h**

https://github.com/Ajmaleee/CircuitShelf

(Added GitHub repo here since only 1 repo is allowed in the main tab)

This is a software subsystem of the hardware I made. The software is a web app hosted at circuitshelf.pages.dev. The function of this website is the same as that of the hardware subsystem: to track modules I own.

![Screenshot_20261003-133609](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/rWl10s59mLisg4XtHMiy6Tgh5DzAJl32/9a2e3c93a05e5bb64b21c236efab624c6c80f5518c99efdc27aef36c14a5a3ef.png)

![Screenshot_20261003-133449](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/rWl10s59mLisg4XtHMiy6Tgh5DzAJl32/a303ac91f97a6543b5b791ec5eece8af491e0319c1433ac54e08955c79c54d23.png)

Why do I need a software subsystem? Let’s say I’m not at home or don’t currently have access to my hardware subsystem. If a random idea pops into my head and I want to know the locations of the modules I have stored and whether those modules are available to me, I can go to circuitshelf.pages.dev. From there, I can scroll through my modules and see whether each module is working, not working, or untested. I can also lend and receive these items.

Here’s a guide on how to navigate the webpage.

When entering the webpage, you will be greeted with two cards: Parts and Add Part and Load Starter Kits.

Currently, the website you have accessed is local. If you want to connect it to the Firebase Firestore server I have set up, go to the three dots in the lowermost-right corner and click the Sync Password option under Sync Across Devices. You can press that button and set up a password.

![Screenshot_20261003-133503](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/rWl10s59mLisg4XtHMiy6Tgh5DzAJl32/5bce63884d9e714dbd92421b5f97529d4323e5164d5025d1a95df8c12e1c7bc3.png)

Here’s the thing: different users can set different passwords. Let’s say I set my password as 123 on my mobile, then went to my brother’s mobile and typed the password 123—the same password I entered on my other device. It will log me into the same Firebase-connected account, allowing me to see the modules. This also prevents other people from accessing my files and using malicious code against my Firebase, since I have not included much security right now.

If you would like to see the modules I have, please message me at ajmalsworkshop@gmail.com. I will send you the details needed to view them.

If you would like to test out this webpage, you can go to Add Part and enter the necessary details to add your modules. This website will keep track of each module and the total amount you spend on it.the below images shows the categories  (lent out working,untested)

![Screenshot_20261003-133649](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/rWl10s59mLisg4XtHMiy6Tgh5DzAJl32/47861e0fb71de186f6b44c5202b791c4b8b3b10c94b4e285759789d5e2c6dafd.png)

![Screenshot_20261003-133642](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/rWl10s59mLisg4XtHMiy6Tgh5DzAJl32/4054618be5d686c2e68115ea598869cf74949a0441c0df3cdff192507044f50a.png)

![Screenshot_20261003-133634](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/rWl10s59mLisg4XtHMiy6Tgh5DzAJl32/f2ebd3bfc1c769bbef5b24086851e91cd58ad9cfd1d7251ca6fdcd3eb496d8f1.png)

Under Settings, you can add many modules at once, load a starter kit, and install the website as a PWA. A PWA is a web app that is installed on your mobile phone.

You can also enable Ask for Password on Open so that anyone else accessing your device cannot access your vault.

Below that, you have color palettes. One of my favorites is the rightmost black palette, which has an aesthetic look. However, for better visibility, you need to change the text color below to black. This will give you better visibility.

Below that, we have the Categories tab, where we have sensor modules, boards, actuators, and more. You can also add a category.

Currently, the currency is set to INR, or Indian rupees, by default. However, you can set it to any country’s currency. Almost 10 countries are available right now.

Next, we have Export Backup and Export Spreadsheet, followed by Import Backup. At the lowermost part, you can see Delete All Vaults, which allows you to reset the entire vault.

To install,
click share-add to home screen in ios
Click install from the banner in android
(Same for win,mac,linux)

This is how the installed app showed up on ur home screen

![Screenshot_20261003-133436 1](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/rWl10s59mLisg4XtHMiy6Tgh5DzAJl32/7b458368cba79706c4e754a12c541571c649bddb432f16a3cce85eea627c4e0b.png)

That's it!
